title: Reliability field sprint and stakeholder diary
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, execution-focused journal for a 90-day cross-functional reliability initiative targeting our primary inference surfaces (hosted API + Dedicated routing). The emphasis: rapid, measurable SLO experiments, clear stakeholder obligations, and an ops-ready cutover path.

High-level objective:
- Reduce user-facing 95th percentile latency by 20% and reduce the frequency of transient request failures that contribute to SLO breaches by 40% for text generation routes within 90 days while keeping cost delta < 5%.

Scope (in scope / out of scope):
- In scope: text/generation routes for hosted API and Dedicated default pool; routing fallbacks; KV/prefix cache tuning; autoscaler safety thresholds; alert/triage pipeline.
- Out of scope (this run): embeddings pipeline, billing model change, infra-wide kernel work requiring more than 2-week lead.

Primary stakeholders (Rough):
- Product: Rita Gomez (owned product success metrics)
- Engineering (Serving runtime): Luca Patel (runtime experiments + rollout)
- Observability: Samir Khan (telemetry, dashboards, tracing)
- Platform/Infra: Helen Park (autoscaler + capacity config)
- Customer Success: Priya Das (customer impact comms)
- SRE lead / facilitator: Maya Chen (this doc owner)

Success criteria (how we’ll measure success):
- SLO metrics: 95th percentile tail latency for generation <= target_ms (target_ms noted in sprint). Error-rate contributing to SLO (5xx + client-visible timeouts) down 40% vs baseline.
- Operational: > 90% of oncall incidents for these routes fall below critical severity after runbook adoption.
- Business: risk-adjusted cost change <= +5%.

Baseline & instrumentation checklist (must be green before experiments):
- Baseline dashboard created and pinned: 95th, 99th latency by route; error-class breakdown; traffic distribution by model, seq-len.
- Tracing hooks: end-to-end trace for generation requests with kernel and routing spans.
- Error tagging: failures must include failure-class, model-variant, region.
- Canary metric: synthetic generator that emits a fixed prompt every 10s to test latency and success.

90-day plan (three 30-day phases):
Phase A (Day 0–30): Discover & quick wins
- Goals: validate signals, run small config experiments (cache TTLs, prefix caching heuristics), stabilize autoscaler thresholds.
- Deliverables: experiment matrix, 2 low-risk tuning PRs, runbook draft for observed failure classes.
- Key experiments: reduce cache TTL from 60s->15s for high-hit prefixes (monitor miss-rate), enable lightweight KV-sharing between similar routes (A/B), tighten autoscaler scale-down grace from 120s->45s for bursty pools.

Phase B (Day 31–60): Targeted SLO experiments & routing policy trials
- Goals: run routing policy A/B (latency-first vs cost-first), measure downstream cost impact. Run model-variant fallback policies in production small percent.
- Deliverables: chosen routing policy with rollback window, SLO delta report, annotated incident runbook updates.
- Key experiments: route 5% traffic to latency-first routing for the heaviest tenant; enable automatic fallback to smaller-quantized model when tail latency breaches 95th threshold (with guardrails).

Phase C (Day 61–90): Harden rollouts & operationalize
- Goals: full rollout of winning configs with documented cutover steps and oncall playbooks, exec summary of metrics and recommendations.
- Deliverables: rollout checklist, release notes for customers, final cost/latency tradeoff appendix.

Weekly cadence and meetings (practical):
- Monday: async status update in #reliability-field (template: one-liner, blockers, metric delta).
- Wed 30m sync (engineering + observability + product): quick experiment status, go/no-go signals.
- Fri 60m retro with extended stakeholders every two weeks (capture learning, update runbook).
- Emergency channel: #reliability-ops-bridge (oncall escalation).

Experiment logging template (fill after each run):
- Experiment name:
- Owner:
- Start / end dates:
- Hypothesis (clear and measurable):
- Change implemented (config / code / routing):
- % traffic (canary):
- Metrics captured (baseline vs current):
- Observations (qual & quant):
- Actions (promote / rollback / tune):
- Notes / open questions:

First 6-week tactical checklist (week-by-week, rough):
Week 1:
- Create pinned baseline dashboard + synthetic probe (Samir).
- Runbook skeleton: map top 6 failure fingerprints (Maya + Luca).
- Kickoff doc + stakeholder invite list (Rita).
Week 2:
- Implement TTL cache experiment in prod-candidate (Luca).
- Autoscaler scale-down config to staging (Helen).
- Quick comm with CS on potential customer-visible latencies (Priya).
Week 3:
- Canary TTL experiment at 1% traffic; collect 72h sample (Owners).
- Trace sampling spike checks (Samir).
Week 4:
- Evaluate TTL experiment: decision: promote / tune / rollback.
- Draft routing policy A/B experiment plan (Rita + Luca).
Week 5:
- Launch routing policy A/B at 2% traffic; monitor cost/latency.
- Prepare oncall runbook updates with play examples.
Week 6:
- Interim review: 30-day report to execs (1-pager + dashboard).
- Decide on phase B choices and formalize rollout gates.

Roles, ownership, and quick RACI notes:
- Experiment design: Luca (R), Samir (C), Rita (A), Maya (I)
- Metrics & dashboards: Samir (R), product (C), SRE (I)
- Rollout approvals: Product + SRE lead (A), Platform (C)
- Customer comms: Customer Success (R), Product (C)

Risk register (top 6):
- Regressions in tail quality after quantized fallbacks -> mitigation: gated 0.5% traffic canary + automated quality eval using eval-set.
- Autoscaler flapping causing cold starts -> mitigation: conservative scaling/ghost-instance warmers + abort window.
- Observability blind spots -> mitigation: short-term increased trace sampling for routes under test, alert if sampling drops.
- Customer surprise on latency variance -> mitigation: proactive CS emails + opt-out flag for affected tenants.
- Cost overshoot -> mitigation: cost monitor alert + automatic rollback after spend delta threshold.
- Runbook not adopted by oncall -> mitigation: 1:1 pairing sessions and runbook-driven pager drills.

Rollout gating criteria (must be met before promoting experiment cluster-wide):
- No >10% increase in model output regressions on eval-set (quality check).
- 7-day moving average for 95th latency improved or neutral vs baseline.
- Cost delta within agreed bounds or explained with mitigation plan.
- Runbook updates reviewed and acknowledged by oncall owners.

Oncall play (quick reference):
- Symptom: sudden tail latency spike (>2x 95th baseline)
  - Step 1: Check canary synthetic probe and trace sampling (Samir).
  - Step 2: Identify recent config merges / experiment flags (Luca).
  - Step 3: If routing policy in play, roll traffic to conservative path (Helen).
  - Step 4: If still unresolved after 15m, escalate to SRE lead and open incident channel.

Open questions / decisions to confirm (live list):
- What exact ms target for 95th percentile do we commit to per route? (Product to propose)
- Acceptable cost delta per tenant vs aggregate? (Finance/Product)
- Do we need an explicit customer opt-out for model-variant fallback? (Legal/CS)
- Who owns post-rollout quality regression monitoring (product or applied-ml)?

Notes to self / loose ideas (brain-dump):
- Could we run a parallel synthetic test harness that mimics high concurrency with warm cache distribution? Would make cache experiments more predictive.
- Consider temporary high-sample tracing per region for 72h after each promotion. Costy but buys signal.
- Try an "error budget sprint" hackweek with feature teams to clear top 10 incident contributors.

End of doc.

(Version notes: draft v0.3 — will update after first 30-day review. This is intentionally pragmatic: aim for experiments that have clear guardrails and immediate rollback paths. Keep CS loop tight.)
